thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: HIGH - Authentication service: token validation errors > 10% across prod clusters. Pager: pagerduty-bot. Incident ID: PD-93217.

pagerduty-bot: Triggered on: auth.jwt.verify.failure rate spike, threshold 10% per 5m. Affected services: api-gateway (us-east-1), auth-service (auth-primary). Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-93217

maya: acked. I'm oncall. Starting triage — what are we seeing? :wave:

alex: saw a big uptick in 401s at 14:12 UTC from api-gateway. Logs show signature failures: 
```
2026-03-14T14:12:18Z api-gw-1 ERROR token_verification failed: invalid signature, kid=key_2026_03_14_v2
2026-03-14T14:12:19Z api-gw-2 ERROR token_verification failed: kid not found in JWKS, token.kid=key_2026_03_14_v2
2026-03-14T14:12:20Z auth-svc-3 WARN jwks_fetch error: 404 on https://auth.redwood.internal/.well-known/jwks.json
```

sam: any recent key rotations?

jen: yes, the automated rotation job ran at 14:10 UTC — rotated signing key to `key_2026_03_14_v2` and pushed JWKS to KMS-backed store. I saw a couple of warnings earlier about JWKS propagation to edge caches failing.

alex: looks like api-gateway and auth-service caches still expect older `key_2026_03_01_v1`. The token issuer is handing out tokens signed with v2, but the JWKS served to some zones hasn't been updated.

maya: impact? which customers / endpoints?

alex: spike in 401s mostly for token-authenticated endpoints: /v1/streams, /v1/generate. Error rate peaked at 28% for runtime tokens; internal services using mTLS unaffected. Some customers on Dedicated saw failures via us-east-1 region.

sam: can we force JWKS reload or fallback to previous key? What's fastest mitigation?

jen: two options: 1) revert rotation (re-sign with old key) — risky if new key already in use; 2) force JWKS propagation to edge caches and add old key to current JWKS (include both keys) — safer and fast. I'll try updating the JWKS to include both v1 and v2.

maya: do it. Post exact commands here so we can track. Also set incident severity and notify SRE + support.

jen: running rollout: 
```
# fetch current jwks from store
curl -sS "https://kms-store.internal/jwks/auth-service" > /tmp/jwks_before.json
# append old key into new JWKS and push
python tools/jwks_merge.py /tmp/jwks_before.json /opt/keys/old_key_v1.json > /tmp/jwks_combined.json
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KMS_TOKEN" -d @/tmp/jwks_combined.json https://kms-store.internal/jwks/auth-service
# trigger auth-service config reload
kubectl -n auth rollout restart deployment/auth-service
```

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Updated incident PD-93217 with status: mitigation in progress. Escalation timer paused.

alex: after pushing combined JWKS and restarting auth-service, I'm seeing JWKS fetch success in logs and gateway validation errors dropping.

```
2026-03-14T14:15:42Z auth-svc-1 INFO jwks_fetch success: 200, keys=2
2026-03-14T14:15:55Z api-gw-2 INFO token_verification succeeded: kid=key_2026_03_14_v2
```

maya: monitor error rate and latency. Sam, can you notify support + customers with known impact? Put a brief note on status.redwood.ai and escalate to enterprise success for Dedicated customers.

sam: on it. Drafting status update: 
"We experienced elevated 401 errors for token-authenticated endpoints caused by a JWKS propagation issue following a scheduled key rotation. We have rolled back to a dual-key JWKS allowing both previous and new tokens to validate. Authentication service is showing normal error rates. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a postmortem."

pagerduty-bot: Note added to PD-93217: mitigation pushed, service recovery observed.

jen: metrics show error rate down to 1.2% (was 28%). Request latency unaffected. Killing remaining old gateway caches via cache-invalidate job now.

alex: running cache invalidation: 
```
POST https://edge-cache.us-east-1.internal/invalidate
{ "paths": ["/.well-known/jwks.json"], "zone": "*" }
```

maya: confirmed reduction to baseline. Marking incident as resolved soon but keep monitoring for 1 hour before close. Create postmortem doc and capture follow-ups:
- add pre-rotation check to ensure JWKS propagated to all edge caches
- add monitoring for key mismatch errors (kid not found) with alert threshold lower than 10%
- make rotation-safe (publish dual-key JWKS prior to switching issuer)

sam: created status page entry and emailed Enterprise Success for affected Dedicated customers.

jen: filed follow-up PR to rotation pipeline to publish dual-key JWKS 5 minutes before switch and to run a propagation check.

maya: thanks everyone. Incident resolved -> monitoring. I'll set severity to Sev2 and kick off postmortem template. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: PD-93217 status: Resolved (mitigation applied). Close reason: JWKS propagation mismatch after automated key rotation; dual-key JWKS roll forward applied.

alex: quick note — we should consider making key rotation a canary job per region next.

sam: +1. I'll add to backlog. :thumbsup:

maya: handing off to postmortem owners (jen, alex). Oncall clear in 15.

jen: oncall acknowledged handoff.

maya: last check: any lingering errors?

alex: none in the last 5m. closing in 30.

sam: Thanks all — great quick coordinated response.
